content: Eric Swedberg, representing Save the Children, is based in New York, United States. Yara Sfeir is affiliated with Action Against Hunger/Action Contre la Faim in Paris, France. Samira Aboubaker works in the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health at the World Health Organization (WHO) in Geneva, Switzerland. France Bégin is associated with the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) in New York, United States. Geoffrey Bisoborwa is part of the WHO Regional Office for Africa in Brazzaville, Congo. Caroline Bollars is with the WHO Representative Office for Samoa. Rachida Bouhouch is also part of the WHO Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health in Geneva, Switzerland. Dilberth Cordero is affiliated with the Pan American Health Organization in Honduras. Férima Coulibaly-Zerbo works at the WHO Country Office in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Peggy Henderson is part of the WHO Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health. Karimen León Flández is also associated with the same department at WHO. Several individuals were invited but could not attend. These include Suzanne Farhoud from the WHO Country Office in Cairo, Egypt, and Lynda Kiess from the World Food Programme. Technical experts who participated in the guideline scoping meeting on March 18–19, 2013, included Maharaj K. Bhan, a professor of child health in Delhi, India; James Berkley from the KEMRI/Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Kilifi, Kenya; Caroline H.D. Fall from the MRC Lifecourse Epidemiology Unit at the University of Southampton, United Kingdom; Sanjay Kinra from the Department of Non-Communicable Disease Epidemiology at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, United Kingdom; Simon Murch from Warwick Medical School, United Kingdom; Shane Norris from the MRC/Wits Developmental Pathways for Health Research Unit at the University of the Witwatersrand, South Africa; John Reilly from the University of Strathclyde, Glasgow, United Kingdom; Harshpal S. Sachdev from the Sitaram Bhartia Institute of Science and Research in New Delhi, India; Susan Sawyer from the University of Melbourne, Australia; and Cesar Victora from the Federal University of Pelotas, Brazil. The WHO Steering Committee in Geneva, Switzerland, included Rajiv Bahl from the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health; Mercedes de Onis, Chizuru Nishida, and Juan Pablo Peña-Rosas from the Department of Nutrition for Health and Development; Nigel Rollins from the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health; Zita C. Weise Prinzo from the Department of Nutrition for Health and Development; and Wilson Were from the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health. WHO acknowledges the technical input of Amit Agarwal from the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research in Chandigarh, India, in preparing systematic reviews and data analyses. The Guideline Development Group and Advisory Groups included Aluisio Barros from the Federal University of Pelotas, Brazil; Ruth M. Bland from the Royal Hospital for Sick Children, University of Glasgow, United Kingdom; Andrew Connelly from the Medical School, University of Glasgow, United Kingdom; Nishant Jaiswal from the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, India; Anne Martin from the University of Strathclyde, Glasgow, United Kingdom; Liesl Nicol from the Centre for Evidence-Based Health Care, Stellenbosch University, South Africa; John J. Reilly (team lead) from the University of Strathclyde, Glasgow, United Kingdom; Meenu Singh (team lead) from the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, India; Kiran Kumar Thumburu from the same institution; Cesar Victora from the Federal University of Pelotas, Brazil; Marianne Visser from Stellenbosch University, South Africa; and Taryn Young (team lead) from Stellenbosch University, South Africa. External peer-review experts included Ameena Goga from the Medical Research Council, South Africa; Marko Kerac from the Institute of Child Health, University College London, United Kingdom; Marie McGrath from the Emergency Nutrition Network, London, United Kingdom; and Rebecca Norton from the International Baby Food Action Network, Geneva, Switzerland. The WHO Steering Committee approved declarations of interest in October 2014. Linda Adair from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, United States, declared that her institution received funding from Wyeth in 2012 and from 2012 to 2014, which was later acquired by Nestlé in 2013. However, Dr. Adair did not personally receive any funds. André Briend, formerly of the University of Tampere, Finland, declared no conflicts of interest. Suzanne Farhoud, a former regional adviser for child and adolescent health at WHO’s Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean, also declared no conflicts. Rukhsana Haider from the World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action and Training and Assistance for Health and Nutrition (THAN) Foundation declared no conflicts. Alan Jackson from the University of Southampton, United Kingdom, declared no conflicts. Zein Karrar from the University of Khartoum, Sudan, declared no conflicts. Cecilia Martinez-Costa from the University of Valencia, Spain, declared no conflicts. John Reilly from the University of Strathclyde, United Kingdom, declared a conflict of interest.
